q: What type of foundation is recommended to prevent impact on adjacent structures during construction?
n: Sheet piling retains the excavation sides so digging does not undermine adjacent structures. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering; DOLE OSHS (excavation).

q: Which foundation least disturbs an adjoining high-rise on flat ground?
n: Bored (cast-in-place) piles avoid the vibration and heave of driven piles, so they least disturb an adjoining high-rise. Source: Tomlinson, Pile Design and Construction Practice.

q: What type of footing is typically used along property lines?
n: At property lines a column footing cannot project past the line, so a combined (or strap) footing keeps the load centred. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: What footing usually supports a bearing wall?
n: Bearing walls are usually supported on a continuous strip footing. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What type of foundation is commonly used for a project located on a 35% sloping site?
n: On steep slopes such as 35%, isolated footings tied with tie beams step with the terrain and resist lateral spread. Source: NSCP 2015, Chapter 3; Ching.

q: What type of foundation is typically used for residential projects built on hard soil?
n: On hard soil, residential projects typically use simple isolated (spread) footings. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: What type of foundation is most suitable for adobe soil?
n: Adobe (soft volcanic tuff) is firm, competent bearing material, so simple isolated footings suffice. Source: Das; Philippine geotechnical practice (Guadalupe tuff).

q: What type of footing is recommended for sloping sites?
n: Sloping sites use stepped footings (walls) or isolated footings set at stepped levels. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which footing suits soft soil best?
n: On soft soil a mat foundation lowers bearing pressure and differential settlement. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: What strip footing changes level in steps to suit a slope or varying strata?
n: A stepped footing is a strip footing that changes level in steps to suit a slope or varying strata. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What do you call the continuous spread footing used to support a foundation wall?
n: A strip (wall) footing is the continuous spread footing under a foundation wall. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What cast-in-place foundation is made by boring or hand-digging a shaft to a bearing stratum and filling it with concrete?
n: A pier (drilled pier) is a cast-in-place foundation made by boring or hand-digging a shaft to bearing strata and filling it with concrete. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What foundation wall encloses usable space below a building?
n: A basement wall is a foundation wall enclosing usable space below a building. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which is a shallow foundation?
n: Isolated (spread) footings are shallow foundations. Piles and caissons are deep. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: What is the hard pointed or rounded tip of a pile that pierces the soil?
n: The shoe is the hard pointed or rounded tip fitted to a pile so it pierces the soil. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What equipment drives piles?
n: A pile hammer (drop, diesel or hydraulic) drives piles. Source: Tomlinson, Pile Design and Construction Practice.

q: What fills the hole of a bored pile after drilling?
n: After drilling, a bored pile hole is filled with concrete around a rebar cage. Source: Tomlinson, Pile Design and Construction Practice.

q: What transfers the column load to a group of piles?
n: A pile cap transfers the column load to a group of piles. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: What iron weight is raised and dropped to drive a pile?
n: A drop hammer is an iron weight raised and dropped to drive a pile. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Where can you typically find the details for foundation anchor bolts?
n: Anchor bolt layouts and details are shown on the foundation plan. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; AISC Design Guide 1.

q: What usually happens to a footing when it begins to deform?
n: Upward soil pressure bends the footing's projections upward like cantilevers, putting tension at the bottom. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 413.2.7; Das.

q: What can happen when a column rests on a footing that is not reinforced with rebars?
o: The footing will crack at an angle
The column will punch through the footing
n: An unreinforced footing under a concentrated column load cracks diagonally from shear and flexure, failing at an angle. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 413; ACI 318 commentary.

q: Which aggregate has a dry loose weight of 1,120 kg/m³ or less?
n: Lightweight aggregate has a dry loose bulk density of 1,120 kg/m³ or less (fine 1,120, coarse 880). Source: ASTM C330.

q: What secures a column base plate to the foundation against uplift and shear?
n: Anchor bolts cast into the pier secure a column base plate against uplift and shear. Source: AISC Design Guide 1.

q: What is the purpose of rebar (reinforcement) in a concrete footing?
n: Footing reinforcement resists the bending tension from soil pressure and, with adequate depth, helps the footing resist punching shear around the column. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 413.

q: What is the main job of reinforcement in concrete?
n: Reinforcement mainly resists tensile stress, because concrete is weak in tension. Source: PCA; NSCP 2015 Chapter 4.

q: Which footing is used when two columns are so close that separate footings would overlap?
n: When two columns are so close that separate footings would overlap, a combined footing carries both. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: In yielding soil, which raft foundation is set deep enough that the excavated soil weighs as much as the building?
n: A floating foundation is a raft set deep enough that the weight of excavated soil roughly equals the building's weight. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: What system of end-bearing or friction piles, caps and tie beams carries loads to a firm stratum?
n: A pile foundation, of end-bearing or friction piles with caps and tie beams, carries loads to a firm stratum. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: What interlocking sheets are driven against earth in swampy or unstable ground?
n: Sheet piles are interlocking sheets driven to retain earth and water in swampy or unstable ground. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: What is a pile driven at an angle to resist lateral and uplift forces?
n: A battered (raked) pile is driven at an angle to resist lateral and uplift forces. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: On weak soil, which foundation best spreads a heavy building load?
n: On weak soil a mat best spreads a heavy building load, lowering bearing pressure. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: Which soil has the weakest bearing capacity?
n: Peat, highly organic and compressible, has the weakest bearing capacity. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 304-1 (presumptive load-bearing values); Das.

q: What foundation links two column footings with a beam?
n: A strap footing links two column footings with a rigid beam (strap) that balances eccentric loads. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: According to the Building Code, what is the minimum thickness of a footing?
n: The NBC requires dwelling footings at least 250 mm thick and 600 mm below the ground surface. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 708.
